newsitem.title: USA: NBA-BUCKS BASKETBALL CHIEF DUNLEAVY RESIGNS.
newsitem.headline: NBA-BUCKS BASKETBALL CHIEF DUNLEAVY RESIGNS.

text.p: Mike Dunleavy resigned on Saturday as vice president of basketball operations and general manager of the Milwaukee Bucks, who missed the playoffs for the sixth straight season.
The Bucks finshed 33-49 (.402) and in seventh place in the Central Division this season.
It was an eight-game improvement from last season, when the club had just 25 wins under Dunleavy, who was fired as head coach a year ago. Chris Ford was later hired as head coach.
Dunleavy was under an eight-year contract that was to take him through the 1999-2000 season, but he called it quits because he was unable to turn the club into playoff material.

"I have enjoyed my five years in Milwaukee," Dunleavy said. "The Bucks have been great. I am sorry that I did not get to accomplish what I and the organisation wanted to -- get back into the playoffs. I am not sorry I took the opportunity, I do regret that I did not succeed."

In four seasons as Milwaukee's head coach, Dunleavy compiled a 107-221 (.326) record. He was 101-63 (.616) as coach of the Los Angeles Lakers, whom he led to an NBA Finals loss against the Chicago Bulls in 1990-91 before joining the Bucks.

In 1991-92, his first season with the Bucks, Dunleavy was 28-54. They were 20-62 the following season and selected Vin Baker in the NBA Draft. After the 1993-94 season, the Bucks won the lottery and picked Glenn Robinson.

Prior to this season, Milwaukee had the fourth pick in the draft and selected point guard Stephon Marbury, but traded him to Minnesota for fifth pick Ray Allen and a future number one choice. Marbury helped lead Minnesota to the playoffs.
